--- title: "Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns" subtitle: "Quantifying diversity and modelling distributions in R" author: "Your Name" format: revealjs bibliography: references.bib --- ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(sf); library(terra) library(vegan); library(betapart); library(iNEXT) library(predicts); library(blockCV); library(usdm) library(tidyverse); library(patchwork); library(viridis) theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13)) ``` ::: ## Quantifying Biodiversity {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## The α, β, γ Framework Following @whittaker1972evolution: $$ \gamma = \alpha \times \beta $$ | Component | Scale | R function | |-------------|----------------------|-------------------------| | α (alpha) | Local richness | `vegan::specnumber()` | | β (beta) | Turnover among sites | `betapart::beta.pair()` | | γ (gamma) | Regional richness | `vegan::specpool()` | ## Hill Numbers — A Unified Framework $$ {}^{q}\!D = \left( \sum_{i=1}^{S} p_i^{\,q} \right)^{1/(1-q)} $$ - \(q = 0\): species richness - \(q = 1\): exponential of Shannon entropy - \(q = 2\): inverse Simpson concentration ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(iNEXT) out <- iNEXT(community_data, q = c(0, 1, 2), datatype = "abundance", endpoint = 500) ggiNEXT(out, type = 1) + scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D") ``` ::: ## α-Diversity Example ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(vegan) data(BCI) # tropical tree community div <- tibble( site = rownames(BCI), S = specnumber(BCI), H = diversity(BCI, index = "shannon"), Simpson = diversity(BCI, index = "simpson"), Pielou_J = H / log(S) ) div |> pivot_longer(-site) |> ggplot(aes(value)) + geom_histogram(fill = "#4A7C59", bins = 20) + facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free") ``` ::: ## β-Diversity: Turnover vs Nestedness @baselga2010partitioning decomposed Sørensen β into two components: $$ \beta_{\text{SOR}} = \beta_{\text{SIM}} + \beta_{\text{SNE}} $$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(betapart) # Convert abundance to presence/absence pa <- ifelse(BCI > 0, 1, 0) # Pairwise multi-component beta bp <- beta.pair(pa, index.family = "sorensen") # Mean values sapply(bp, mean) #> beta.sim beta.sne beta.sor #> 0.41 0.06 0.47 ``` ::: ## Visualising β-Diversity ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ape) # UPGMA on turnover hc <- hclust(bp$beta.sim, method = "average") # NMDS ordination nmds <- metaMDS(bp$beta.sor, k = 2, trymax = 50) plot(nmds, type = "t", main = "NMDS — Sørensen dissimilarity") ``` ::: ## Species Distribution Modelling {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## SDM Workflow ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A[Cleaned
occurrences] --> C[Predictor
selection] B[Environmental
layers] --> C C --> D[Pseudo-absences
or background] D --> E[Model fitting] E --> F[Spatial
cross-validation] F --> G[Prediction &
uncertainty] style G fill:#4A7C59,color:white ``` ## Predictor Selection — Multicollinearity ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(usdm) # Variance Inflation Factor stepwise selection v <- vifstep(bio_gr, th = 5) v #> 4 variables from 19 input variables have collinearity problem: #> bio6 bio11 bio16 bio17 # Keep only retained predictors preds <- bio_gr[[v@results$Variables]] ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip} A VIF threshold of **5–10** is common; lower is stricter. ::: ## Background / Pseudo-absences ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(predicts) # 10,000 random background points within Greece set.seed(42) bg <- spatSample(preds, size = 10000, method = "random", na.rm = TRUE, as.points = TRUE, values = FALSE) # Extract environmental values at presence + background pres_env <- extract(preds, vect(pts_thin)) bg_env <- extract(preds, bg) train <- bind_rows( mutate(pres_env, occ = 1), mutate(as_tibble(bg_env), occ = 0) ) |> drop_na() ``` ::: ## Fitting a MaxEnt-style Model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(predicts) # MaxEnt via the `predicts` package (successor of `dismo`) mod <- MaxEnt( x = preds, p = st_coordinates(pts_thin), removeDuplicates = TRUE ) # Predict habitat suitability suit <- predict(preds, mod, type = "cloglog") plot(suit, col = viridis(100), main = "Habitat suitability") ``` ::: ## Spatial Block Cross-Validation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(blockCV) sb <- cv_spatial( x = pts_thin, column = "occ", k = 5, size = 50000, # 50 km blocks selection = "random", iteration = 100 ) cv_plot(cv = sb, x = pts_thin) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important} Random CV inflates SDM performance by exploiting spatial autocorrelation. **Always use spatial blocking** for honest evaluation. ::: ## Model Evaluation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(predicts) eval_metrics <- pa_evaluate( p = predict(mod, pres_env_test), a = predict(mod, bg_env_test) ) eval_metrics #> AUC : 0.87 #> COR : 0.42 #> max TSS: 0.61 ``` ::: ## Biogeographical Regionalisation {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## From β-Diversity to Bioregions The workflow: 1. Build a site × species matrix on a regular grid 2. Compute pairwise β-diversity (`betapart`) 3. Apply hierarchical clustering (`hclust`) 4. Cut the dendrogram → bioregions 5. Map back to space ::: aside See @kreft2010framework and @daru2020endemism for ecoregion delineation methods. ::: ## Gridded β-Diversity in R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Build a 0.5° grid grid <- st_make_grid(greece, cellsize = 0.5, square = TRUE) |> st_as_sf() |> mutate(cell_id = row_number()) # Join occurrences to grid sp_grid <- st_join(all_species_pts, grid) # Site × species matrix mat <- sp_grid |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(cell_id, species) |> pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |> column_to_rownames("cell_id") # Presence/absence + Simpson dissimilarity pa <- ifelse(mat > 0, 1, 0) dis <- beta.pair(pa)$beta.sim hc <- hclust(dis, method = "average") clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 5) ``` ::: ## Mapping Bioregions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} grid_clust <- grid |> filter(cell_id %in% rownames(mat)) |> mutate(region = factor(clusters)) ggplot() + geom_sf(data = greece, fill = "grey95") + geom_sf(data = grid_clust, aes(fill = region), color = NA, alpha = 0.85) + scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", name = "Bioregion") + labs(title = "Biogeographical regionalisation of Greece", subtitle = "Based on Simpson β-diversity (turnover)", caption = "Data: GBIF · CRS: EPSG:4326") + theme_void() ``` ::: ## Case Study: Mediterranean Flora {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## Putting It All Together :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Question How is plant β-diversity structured across the Mediterranean basin? ### Data - 25 woody species (GBIF) - WorldClim BIO1, BIO12, BIO15 - SoilGrids texture ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Methods - `rgbif` → retrieval - `CoordinateCleaner` → QC - `betapart` → turnover - `predicts` → SDM - `blockCV` → validation ::: :::: ## Hands-on Exercise 2 {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ### 🛠️ Your turn (90 min) 1. Choose 3 species from yesterday's exercise 2. Stack their cleaned occurrences 3. Build a site × species matrix on a 0.25° grid 4. Compute pairwise β with `betapart::beta.pair()` 5. Cluster and map 2–4 bioregions 6. Discuss: do they align with known phytogeographical zones? ⏱️ Reconvene at **15:00** for synthesis ## Synthesis & Take-aways - R offers a complete, reproducible pipeline for spatial ecology - Choose biodiversity metrics that **match your question**, not vice-versa - SDMs are powerful but require **honest evaluation** (spatial CV) - Biogeographical patterns emerge from β-diversity **structure** - Document, version, share → **open science is good science** ## Further Reading - @lovelace2019geocomputation — Geocomputation with R - @pebesma2023spatial — Spatial Data Science with R - @baselga2010partitioning — β-diversity partitioning - @valavi2021modelling — modern SDM best practices - @whittaker1972evolution — α/β/γ framework ::: {.callout-tip} ## Repository Slides, code, and data: [github.com/yourusername/seminar-patras](https://github.com/yourusername/seminar-patras) ::: ## Thank You! {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ### Ευχαριστώ πολύ! - 📧 kkougiou@aua.gr - 🐙 github.com/kkougiou - 🆔 ORCID: 0000-0002-6938-3025 - 🌐 kkougiou.github.io *Questions, collaborations, follow-ups — always welcome.* ## References ::: {#refs} :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
